# sillydev

The JavaScript and TypeScript client for the [Silly Development](https://sillydev.co.uk) panel API:
start, stop and restart your bots, send console commands, manage files and backups, and deploy from
Git, all from your own code. It also comes with a `sillydev` command line tool, an MCP server for
AI assistants, and opt-in [application monitoring](#monitoring-opt-in).

Full API docs: <https://sillydev.co.uk/docs/panel>

## Install

```sh
npm install sillydev
```

Node.js 18 or later (it uses the built-in `fetch`), Bun or Deno. No runtime dependencies. ES modules
and CommonJS are both supported, and TypeScript types are included.

## Quick start

Create an API key in the panel under **Account, API keys** and put it in the `SILLYDEV_API_KEY`
environment variable. Keys start with `sdevc_` (older `ptlc_` keys keep working).

```ts
import { SillyDev } from 'sillydev';

const client = new SillyDev(); // or new SillyDev({ apiKey: 'sdevc_...' })

for await (const server of client.panel.servers.list()) {
    console.log(server.identifier, server.name);
}

await client.panel.servers.power('1a7ce997', 'restart');
await client.panel.servers.command('1a7ce997', 'say Back in a minute');
```

CommonJS works the same way: `const { SillyDev } = require('sillydev');`.

Each server has an 8-character identifier, shown in the panel and in the `identifier` field of every
server. Every method takes it (or the full UUID) as its first argument.

## Examples

```ts
const panel = client.panel;
const server = '1a7ce997';

// Live state and resource use
const stats = await panel.servers.resources(server);
console.log(stats.current_state, stats.resources.memory_bytes);

// Restart and wait until it's running again (throws WaitTimeoutError after 120 seconds)
await panel.servers.restart(server);
await panel.servers.waitForState(server, 'running', { timeout: 120_000 });

// Files
for (const file of await panel.files.list(server, '/')) {
    console.log(file.name, file.size);
}
const config = await panel.files.read(server, '/config.json');
await panel.files.write(server, '/config.json', config.replace('debug', 'info'));

// Backups
const backup = await panel.backups.create(server, { name: 'before-update' });

// Deploy the linked Git repository
const deployment = await panel.git.deploy(server);
console.log(deployment.status); // "queued"

// Startup variables
await panel.startup.setVariable(server, 'MAIN_FILE', 'bot.js');
```

### Responses and types

Methods resolve to plain objects and arrays. The API's `{"object": ..., "attributes": {...}}`
envelopes are removed, so `(await panel.servers.get(server)).name` just works.

Request bodies and responses are typed from the API's OpenAPI description. Friendly names such as
`Server`, `Backup`, `FileObject` and `GitDeployment` are exported, and every operation's raw shapes
are under the `api` namespace (`api.CreateScheduleBody`, `api.GetBillingResponse` and so on).

### Pagination

`panel.servers.list()`, `panel.backups.list()`, `panel.servers.activity()` and
`panel.account.activity()` return async iterators that fetch the next page as you go. Use
`for await`, or `.toArray()` for everything at once. For one page at a time, with the list's `meta`,
use the `listPage()` and `activityPage()` methods:

```ts
const page = await panel.servers.listPage({ page: 1, perPage: 25 });
console.log(page.total, page.hasNext, page.meta.pending_orders);
```

### Errors

Every error is a `SillyDevError`. Errors the API answers with have their own class:

| Status | Error |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `BadRequestError` |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError` |
| 403 | `PermissionDeniedError` |
| 404 | `NotFoundError` |
| 409 | `ConflictError` |
| 422 | `ValidationError` (`.errors` has every problem, `.fields` groups them by field) |
| 429 | `RateLimitError` (`.retryAfter` in seconds) |
| 5xx | `ServerError` |

If the API cannot be reached at all you get `APIConnectionError`.

```ts
import { ConflictError, NotFoundError } from 'sillydev';

try {
    await panel.servers.restart(server);
} catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ConflictError) {
        console.log('The server is installing or being transferred; try again later');
    } else if (error instanceof NotFoundError) {
        console.log('No such server, or the key cannot reach it');
    } else {
        throw error;
    }
}
```

### Retries and limits

Each account may make 768 requests a minute. Requests answered 429 are retried
twice by default, and reads answered 502, 503 or 504 too (a command or power action is not
repeated, since the server may already have run it), waiting as long as the `Retry-After` header asks. Change it with
`new SillyDev({ maxRetries })`; `0` turns retries off.

Ordering a paid server (`panel.billing.checkout(...)`) always sends an `Idempotency-Key`, so a
retried request never buys twice. Pass `{ idempotencyKey }` yourself to make retries safe across runs.

### Everything else

`client.panel` has one property for each area of the API:

| Property | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| `servers` | list, get, delete, resources, activity, permissions, power, command, share logs, console credentials and relay |
| `console` | the live console and its recent output ([below](#console)) |
| `settings` | rename, reinstall, Docker image, status badge |
| `startup` | startup command and variables |
| `files` | list, read, write, rename, copy, compress, decompress, delete, folders, chmod, pull, signed URLs |
| `backups` | list, create, get, delete, download, lock, restore |
| `schedules` | schedules and their tasks |
| `network` | allocations (ports) |
| `subusers` | other accounts with access to a server |
| `git` | link a repository, deploy, deployments, `sillydev.conf` |
| `account` | the key's account and its activity |
| `serverCreation` | create free servers |
| `databases` | free MariaDB and Postgres databases |
| `billing` | paid servers and subscriptions |
| `monitoring` | monitoring projects, keys, issues, events and usage |

Every method's doc comment names the API operation it calls, so you can look it up in the
[API reference](https://sillydev.co.uk/docs/panel). For anything else, `client.request(method, path,
options)` sends a request with the same key, retries and error handling.

## Console

`client.panel.console` connects to a server's live console: its output, state and resource use as
they happen, with commands and power actions sent back.

```ts
const console = await client.panel.console.connect('1a7ce997');
console.on('console output', ({ args }) => process.stdout.write(args[0] + '\n'));
console.on('status', ({ args }) => process.stdout.write(`[${args[0]}]\n`));
await console.command('say Hello');
await console.power('restart');
// ...
await console.close();
```

Or read it as it comes, from the moment the node accepted the token (leaving the loop closes it):

```ts
for await (const { event, args } of await client.panel.console.connect('1a7ce997')) {
    if (event === 'console output') process.stdout.write(args[0] + '\n');
}
```

The recent output (about the last 150 lines; empty while the server is offline):

```ts
const lines = await client.panel.console.history('1a7ce997');
```

There are four ways to reach a console, and by default (`transport: 'auto'`) each is tried in turn
until one works:

| `transport` | How |
| --- | --- |
| `websocket` | A websocket to the server's node. The quickest. Uses the global `WebSocket` (Node.js 22 or later, Bun); on older Node.js pass `{ WebSocket }` from the [`ws`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ws) package, or `auto` skips it. |
| `stream` | The same messages streamed over plain HTTPS from a session on the node, for networks that block websockets. |
| `poll` | The same session read by long polling, for proxies that hold streams back. |
| `relay` | The panel reads a session on the node for you, for networks that can't reach the node at all. A second or two slower. |

Name one, as in `connect(id, { transport: 'poll' })`, to use only that. `console.transport` says
which is in use. Messages are the websocket's on every way: `{ event, args }` with events such as
`console output`, `status`, `stats` (`args[0]` is JSON), `daemon message` and `install output`;
see [the API reference](https://sillydev.co.uk/docs/panel/servers) for the full list. `send(event,
...args)` sends any of them.

The connection renews its token before it expires and reconnects (trying each way again) if it
drops, up to `maxReconnectAttempts` times in a row (default 5; `reconnect: false` turns it off).
When it gives up, or the server is suspended or deleted, the console ends with a `ConsoleError`
whose `reason` says why (`suspended`, `booting`, `token`, `timeout`, `network`, `deleted`,
`throttled` or `unavailable`): `for await` throws it, `onClose(listener)` receives it, and
`console.closeReason` holds it. When `connect()` itself fails with `auto`, `error.attempts` says
why each way failed.

A console counts towards the 30 console connections a server may have open, and connecting gets a
token from the API (limited to 5 a minute per server), so keep one open rather than connecting
again and again.

## Command line

```sh
export SILLYDEV_API_KEY="sdevc_..."

npx sillydev servers list
npx sillydev status 1a7ce997
npx sillydev power 1a7ce997 restart
npx sillydev command 1a7ce997 "say hi"
npx sillydev logs 1a7ce997
npx sillydev console 1a7ce997
npx sillydev deploy 1a7ce997
npx sillydev files ls 1a7ce997 /src
npx sillydev files cat 1a7ce997 /config.json
npx sillydev backups list 1a7ce997
npx sillydev backups create 1a7ce997 --name before-update
```

Add `--json` to any command for JSON output. `console` follows the console live and sends each line
you type as a command; Ctrl+C stops it. `logs` and `console` take `--transport` (as above).

## MCP server

The MCP server lets an AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and others) check on and
control your servers. It needs the MCP SDK next to this package:

```sh
npm install -g sillydev @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
```

Then add it to your assistant's MCP settings, for example:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sillydev": {
      "command": "sillydev",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": { "SILLYDEV_API_KEY": "sdevc_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

Without a global install, use `"command": "npx"` with
`"args": ["-y", "-p", "sillydev", "-p", "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk", "sillydev", "mcp"]`.

Its tools are: list servers, server status, power action, send command, read console (recent
output), list files, read file, Git deploy and list backups. There is nothing for billing or for deleting anything. Give it a key
limited to the servers and permissions you want the assistant to have.

## Monitoring (opt-in)

**Nothing is collected or sent unless you ask for it.** The client, the CLI and the MCP server never
send monitoring data. Monitoring lives in its own entry point, `sillydev/monitoring`, which the
main `sillydev` entry does not import, and importing it does nothing by itself (no timers, no
listeners, not even an environment variable read). Data is only collected after you call
`monitoring.init()` with a key from a monitoring project in the panel, and it goes only to that
project. Turn it off at any time with `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_DISABLED=1`.

```ts
import { monitoring } from 'sillydev/monitoring';

monitoring.init({ key: process.env.SILLYDEV_MONITORING_KEY, service: 'orders-bot', release: '1.4.2' });

monitoring.increment('orders.created', 1, { plan: 'free' });
monitoring.gauge('queue.size', queue.length);
monitoring.timing('payment.duration', 412);
const result = await monitoring.time('report.build', () => buildReport()); // sync or async
monitoring.event('deploy', { version: '1.4.2' });

try {
    await work();
} catch (error) {
    monitoring.captureException(error, { tags: { command: 'order' }, context: { guild_count: 12 } });
}
```

Server keys start with `sdevm_` and name the ingest address (`sdevm_1_…` sends to
`https://ingest1.sillydev.co.uk`). On a Silly Development server linked to a monitoring project, the
key, service name and environment are already in the server's environment, so `monitoring.init()`
with no arguments is enough.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_KEY` | none: without a key nothing starts |
| `endpoint` | `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_URL` | from the key |
| `service` | `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_SERVICE` | `default` |
| `environment` | `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` |
| `release` | `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_RELEASE` | |
| `enabled` | `SILLYDEV_MONITORING_DISABLED=1` turns it off | `true` |
| `runtimeMetrics` | | `true`: CPU, memory, heap, event loop lag, GC, handles, uptime, and the heartbeat |
| `captureUnhandled` | | `true`: uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections |
| `sampleRate` | | `1` (share of errors and events kept) |
| `beforeSend(type, item)` | | change an item, or return `null` to drop it |
| `flushInterval` | | `10000` ms |
| `maxBufferBytes` | | `1000000` |
| `slowThresholdMs` | | `1000` |
| `debug` | | `false`: logs every payload before it is sent |

Every function is a safe no-op before `init()` (and `time()` still runs your function), and none of
them ever throws into your code. Metrics are added up in memory and sent every 10 seconds, gzipped,
in the background; the timer never keeps your process alive. When the ingest is unreachable, data
is buffered (up to `maxBufferBytes`, oldest dropped first) and retried with backoff; a `429` is
retried after `Retry-After`; a refused key (`401`) or a disabled project (`403`) stops monitoring with
one warning. Tags and context under keys that look like secrets (`password`, `secret`, `token`,
`authorization`, `cookie`, `api_key`) are replaced with `[redacted]`.

`monitoring.flush()` sends everything now, and `monitoring.shutdown()` flushes and stops. Pending
data is sent automatically when the event loop empties; call `await monitoring.shutdown()` before
`process.exit()`.

**Crashes behave exactly as before.** Uncaught exceptions are recorded with
`process.on('uncaughtExceptionMonitor')`, which does not change what Node does. If nothing else will
handle the error, the report is sent synchronously (from a short-lived child process, at most 2
seconds) and Node then prints the error and exits with code 1 as usual. No `uncaughtException`
listener is added, and no `unhandledRejection` listener is added unless your application has one
of its own: with Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw`, an unhandled rejection reaches the
same monitor. (On Bun, and with `--unhandled-rejections=warn` or `none`, unhandled rejections are
only recorded while your application has an `unhandledRejection` listener.)

### Frameworks

None of these frameworks is a dependency. Each records `http.server.duration` (tagged with the
route template, method and status class), slow requests, and server errors.

```ts
// Express
import { monitoringMiddleware, monitoringErrorHandler } from 'sillydev/monitoring/express';
app.use(monitoringMiddleware()); // before your routes
app.use(monitoringErrorHandler()); // after your routes; passes every error on

// Fastify
import { monitoringPlugin } from 'sillydev/monitoring/fastify';
await app.register(monitoringPlugin);

// Hono
import { monitoringMiddleware } from 'sillydev/monitoring/hono';
app.use(monitoringMiddleware());

// discord.js: command durations and outcomes, errors, gateway latency and guild count
import { monitorClient } from 'sillydev/monitoring/discord';
monitorClient(client);
```

### Websites

`sillydev/monitoring/browser` is for web pages and uses a browser key (`sdevb_…`), which is safe to
put in page source; never put a server key in a page. Add your site's origin to the project's
allowed origins in the panel.

```ts
import { monitoring } from 'sillydev/monitoring/browser';

monitoring.init({ key: 'sdevb_1_…', release: '2026.10.1' });
```

It records JavaScript errors, page views (`browser.page_views`, by path with numbers and UUIDs
replaced by `:id`) and web vitals (LCP, CLS, INP, TTFB and FCP), plus anything you send with
`monitoring.event()` and `monitoring.captureException()`. Options: `service` (default `website`),
`environment`, `release`, `sampleRate`, `captureErrors`, `webVitals`, `pageViews`, `beforeSend`
and `debug`. It sets and reads no cookies, never sends query strings, and records no IP addresses
or user identifiers. Data is sent with `navigator.sendBeacon` when the page is hidden and with
`fetch` otherwise.

## Configuration

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apiKey` | `SILLYDEV_API_KEY` | (required) |
| `baseURL` | `SILLYDEV_BASE_URL` | `https://sillydev.co.uk/panel/api/client` |
| `timeout` | | 60000 ms |
| `maxRetries` | | 2 |
| `fetch` | | the global `fetch` |
